title: Plant cover did not resolve a shared nitrogen response eleven years after addition stopped at Culardoch
abstract: We tested whether a former nitrogen response remained in plant composition eleven years after addition stopped at one Scottish alpine heath. We used 22 matched high-dose and control pairs in three blocks from a 2026 data release. Early response directions were learned in other blocks to score each held-out block. The primary late Hellinger alignment was 0.00730, with conditional 95% bootstrap limits -0.00789 to 0.02531. Early alignment was also uncertain, so a point retention ratio of 0.56 was not reliable. Relative cover was unresolved. Recorded occurrence gave a positive late alignment of 0.561 (0.134 to 1.037), and a conditional retention ratio of 0.309 (0.113 to 0.470). Final treatment separation did not pass the three-measure randomization correction for any representation. The results permit a membership legacy but do not establish a shared cover response, full recovery or a cause of the climate-tracking gap. The new test separates historical direction retention from endpoint separation. It extends earlier lichen richness accounting in the same archive. One site, three blocks, a high former dose, recording changes and rescued metadata limit inference. Code, aggregate estimates, a figure, source hashes and independent checks are included. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Early and late response alignment learned in separate field blocks. Bars use different units across panels. Intervals are conditional on three sampled blocks. The cover tests were unresolved; the membership interval was positive, but its endpoint randomization test did not pass correction.
